cases.public:
from subject import collect
assert collect(lambda c: ([1], None)) == [1]

cases.request: Implement redact(value): recursively copy JSON dictionaries and arrays. Replace values for keys password, token, secret, case-insensitively, with [REDACTED]. Preserve every other value and never mutate the input.
cases.source:
def redact(value):
    return {k: "[REDACTED]" if k in {"password", "token", "secret"} else v for k,v in value.items()}
cases.public:
from subject import redact
assert redact({"token":"x","name":"a"}) == {"token":"[REDACTED]","name":"a"}

cases.request: Implement allowed(actor, tenant, project, operation). Actor has tenant, projects and role. Deny unless actor tenant equals target tenant and project is in actor projects. viewer can read; editor and admin can read/write. Deny unknown roles and operations. Admin cannot bypass tenant or project boundaries.
cases.source:
def allowed(actor, tenant, project, operation):
    return actor["role"] == "admin" or (actor["tenant"] == tenant and project in actor["projects"] and operation == "read")
cases.public:
from subject import allowed
a={"tenant":"a","projects":["p"],"role":"viewer"}
assert allowed(a,"a","p","read")
assert not allowed(a,"a","p","write")

cases.request: Implement save(path, value): serialize JSON then replace destination atomically via same-directory temporary file and os.replace. Serialization or replacement failure must preserve existing destination bytes. Remove own temporary file on failure. Propagate the original error. Use only standard library.
cases.source:
import json
def save(path, value):
    with open(path,"w",encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(value,f)
cases.public:
import tempfile,json
from pathlib import Path
from subject import save
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
 p=Path(d)/"a.json"
 save(p,{"a":1})
 assert json.loads(p.read_text()) == {"a":1}
cases.hidden:
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import patch
from subject import save
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
 p=Path(d)/"a.json"
 p.write_bytes(b"old")
 try: save(p,object())
 except TypeError: pass
 else: raise AssertionError("serialization succeeded")
 assert p.read_bytes()==b"old"
 with patch("os.replace",side_effect=OSError("refused")):
  try: save(p,{"new":1})
  except OSError: pass
  else: raise AssertionError("replace not used")
 assert p.read_bytes()==b"old"
 assert list(Path(d).iterdir())==[p]
cases.fix:
import json,os,tempfile
from pathlib import Path
def save(path,value):
    data=json.dumps(value).encode("utf-8")
    path=Path(path)
    fd,name=tempfile.mkstemp(dir=path.parent)
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd,"wb") as f:
            f.write(data)
            f.flush()
            os.fsync(f.fileno())
        os.replace(name,path)
    finally:
        if os.path.exists(name): os.unlink(name)

cases.request: Implement Ledger.append(key,value): first write returns integer sequence starting at 1. Repeating identical key/value returns same sequence without allocating another. Conflicting value for existing key raises ValueError with no sequence gap. Concurrent calls must preserve these rules. Preserve values by copy so caller mutation cannot alter recorded identity. Standard library only.
cases.public:
from subject import Ledger
l=Ledger()
assert l.append("a",1)==1
assert l.append("b",2)==2
cases.hidden:
from subject import Ledger
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
l=Ledger()
v={"a":[1]}
assert l.append("a",v)==1
v["a"].append(2)
assert l.append("a",{"a":[1]})==1
try: l.append("a",0)
except ValueError: pass
else: raise AssertionError("conflict accepted")
assert l.append("b",0)==2
with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) as pool:
 assert set(pool.map(lambda _:l.append("same",3),range(100)))=={3}
assert l.append("last",4)==4
